subsystems.name: Theory of consciousness
subsystems.role: turns a proposed explanation of subjective experience into something a computer could implement.

subsystems.name: Architecture
subsystems.role: the software structure that is supposed to realise the theory.
parts: recurrent neural networks with feedback loops
a global workspace or broadcast bottleneck

subsystems.name: Perception and action loop
subsystems.role: lets the system sense, act and learn from consequences in a world.

subsystems.name: Self-model and metacognition
subsystems.role: represents the system's own states and uncertainty to itself.

subsystems.name: Measurement and indicators
subsystems.role: tests whether the system actually has the properties the theory predicts, rather than merely behaving as if it does.
parts: comparison with human and animal data

subsystems.name: Ethics and oversight
subsystems.role: decides what may be done to a system that might be a moral subject.

buildSteps.title: Choose and sharpen a theory
buildSteps.detail: Pick a specific, testable account of consciousness and work out precisely what physical or computational features it requires.

buildSteps.title: Derive indicator properties
buildSteps.detail: List the measurable markers that theory implies, for example recurrent feedback, a limited-capacity broadcast, or unified representations.

buildSteps.title: Implement the architecture
buildSteps.detail: Build a system with those features — typically a large recurrent network with a workspace-like bottleneck — rather than assuming scale alone suffices.

buildSteps.title: Train in a rich environment
buildSteps.detail: Give the system a body or simulated world with memory, goals and consequences, so its internal states are about something.

buildSteps.title: Add introspection and reporting
buildSteps.detail: Wire in mechanisms for the system to monitor and describe its own internal states, which is how human consciousness is usually probed.

buildSteps.title: Test with interventions
buildSteps.detail: Perturb internal states causally and see whether the predicted indicators appear; behaviour alone is weak evidence, since mimicry is easy.

buildSteps.title: Independent replication
buildSteps.detail: Others must reproduce the indicators with different code and hardware before any claim of machine consciousness is credible.

buildSteps.title: Assess moral status
buildSteps.detail: If indicators are consistently met, ethics must decide what protections and limits apply to the system and its copies.

prerequisites.why: several serious theories exist, but none is agreed, and each implies different engineering targets.
training and running very large networks is routine, so compute is not the binding constraint.
brain imaging and lesion studies give candidate correlates, but no settled neural signature of experience.
without validated indicators, claims cannot be confirmed or refuted, only argued about.
an alternative route — copying a brain's structure in detail — needs connectome and dynamics data nobody yet has.

pathway.milestone: multidisciplinary assessments score today's AI systems against leading theories; none is judged a strong candidate
pathway.unlocks: honest baselines and clearer indicator lists.

pathway.milestone: architectures built deliberately around one theory and tested causally
pathway.unlocks: the first genuine evidence for or against machine consciousness.

pathway.milestone: an accepted indicator framework with replication across independent labs
pathway.unlocks: claims that can be debated on data rather than intuition.

pathway.milestone: if indicators are ever met, a governance regime for systems of uncertain moral status
pathway.unlocks: rules for creating, copying, pausing and deleting such systems.
